sentences.l2: 在招聘市场中，年龄歧视常以隐性方式出现。
sentences.l1: In the job market, age discrimination often appears in hidden forms.

sentences.l2: 许多岗位表面强调经验与稳定，实则把“35岁门槛”当作筛选标准。
sentences.l1: Many positions superficially emphasize experience and stability, but in fact treat the "age-35 threshold" as a screening criterion.

sentences.l2: 求职者一旦进入这一区间，简历可能被快速过滤，面试机会也随之减少。
sentences.l1: Once job seekers enter this range, their résumés may be quickly filtered out, and interview opportunities decrease accordingly.

sentences.l2: 所谓“中年危机”，并非单纯指个人能力下降，而更多是组织在裁员、重组与绩效评估中，对高薪、资深员工采取的谨慎态度。
sentences.l1: The so-called "midlife crisis" does not simply mean a decline in personal ability, but is more a cautious attitude that organizations take toward highly paid, senior employees in layoffs, restructuring and performance evaluations.

sentences.l2: 企业担心成本上升，也担心员工难以接受高强度变化，于是把年龄视为风险信号。
sentences.l1: Companies worry about rising costs, and also worry that employees will find it hard to accept high-intensity change, so they regard age as a risk signal.

sentences.l2: 这种观念忽略了一个事实：经验、判断力与职业稳定性，往往在中年阶段更加成熟。
sentences.l1: This notion overlooks a fact: experience, judgment and career stability are often more mature in middle age.

sentences.l2: 若招聘只偏好年轻面孔，社会将失去大量可迁移的技能与经验。
sentences.l1: If recruitment favors only young faces, society will lose a great deal of transferable skills and experience.

sentences.l2: 要缓解这一问题，需要建立更公平的评估体系，关注岗位所需能力，而非以年龄作为简单标签。
sentences.l1: To ease this problem, a fairer evaluation system needs to be established, one that focuses on the abilities a position requires, rather than using age as a simple label.
